Left out as self-fixes before she helped: 'inti maz'ooj' -> maz'ooja (25:12-25:27), 'biyaz'aju' -> biyaz'aj (33:21), 'baz'aj' -> 'bnz'aj' for مضارع of انزعج (44:28), 'بل أروح' -> 'قبل ما أروح' (39:53), 'أتعبك' -> 'أتعبها' (58:22, she had only prompted 'Her.' for the English), 'باتعب' -> 'أتعب' after لما (59:18). 'لما I make retired' (57:49) is English mid-sentence but he then produced the Arabic himself, so not filed as tier 3. 17:54 'futtuli in besit' is a meta question she did not follow (كيف؟). 19:17 'ma anbisit?' for 'don't enjoy' was accepted by her as ما انبسطت, so not filed. coverage.r2: 00:26-06:10 is English meta-talk about the app (no Arabic from Medi). Medi's Arabic is Latin-transliterated up to ~36:48, then mostly Arabic script. Transcriber garbles several of Amal's Arabic lines (08:57 'سعود' = صوروا, 43:07/43:29 'سيفاء' = عاصفة, 44:24 'مضايقة' = المضارع, 36:44 'زد أن دنع'), and normalises some of Medi's script (44:47 بننزعج, 55:16 شبعان) so the slip she is fixing is not visible. Left out as self-fixes: 'Inti maz'ooj' → maz'ooja (25:27, she only echoed), anbisit→anbisti gender (18:51), باتعب→أتعب after لما (59:18). Note for the bucket file: Amal teaches إذا + بكون (keeps b-) at 53:49 while lamma + أكون was accepted at 55:39; buckets.md B3 says iza drops b-.

r3_note: Pass-2 rulings made with the transcript open. D7 and D13 are the SAME 39:37 row (r1 0905-26 and r2 0905-26); the disputes matcher paired r1's 39:37 row with r2's 39:25 question row. Final: one B18 row at 39:37 (kept under D7), D13 dropped as its duplicate, and r2's 39:25 'هو بيزعج؟' question is not written (a question, not a produced error). The ما تنزعجي cluster (47:38-49:06) collapses to ONE row (D9, t=48:15) - D15 is a stall, D16 the same slip 19 s later, D17 his English restatement of it. One real error in that cluster is NOT in the disputes: 49:06 'matanzajini' for 'don't get annoyed by me' (object -ni on the N-verb) -> Amal 'No.' (49:21) -> 'By me. ما تنزعجي' -> 'Yes. ما تنزعجي مني' (49:38); bucket D2 (انزعج من). By id order it is almost certainly r1 0905-32 / r2 0905-36 and therefore an agreed row; if it is not in the agreed set the merger should add it (grammar, D2, explicit-no, medium). 50:10-51:28 (D10) is pronunciation by Amal's own framing and she accepted his last attempts. Speaker labels look right throughout; no transcript holes around the D-rows except that the engine already wrote شبعان at 55:16 (D18).

rows.medi_said: Did you enjoy, past tense, your time outside? Okay, so isn't it en-enbistee? Did you enjoy?

rows.why: His written and spoken sentence (enbistee wa2tik barra) had no preposition after انبسط; the first thing she went after was that: 'what is missing? It's not انبسطتي' (06:41), he found 'the fee' (06:50), she confirmed في or بـ (06:54) and repeated 'you forgot the double T and the في' at 07:41-07:45.
rows.english: Did you enjoy your time outside?
rows.r3_why: Two distinct errors sit in this one episode (missing في and missing past -t-); both readers wrote both and only swapped which t carries which bucket. The transcript order is: she prompts for the missing في first (06:41-06:54), so the 06:17 row carries D2 and the 06:33 row (D2 below) carries B5, as r2 had it.

rows.medi_said: I think I gotta take that off. Enbas... Oh, I put enbustee. I put enbustee.

rows.why: Past 2fs of انبسط is انبسطتي (stem + -t- + -i); he said enbustee (= the command انبسطي, no -t-) and defended it at 07:03 ('I thought it was enbustee, you remove the A'); she recast انبسطتي (06:38, 07:12), listed انبسطت / انبسطوا (07:18) and named it 'Yes, it is double T ... you forgot the double T' (07:35-07:41); he closed with enbasatee fee wa2tik barra (07:56).
rows.r3_why: Real and separate from D1: the doubled-t past ending is a B5 rule, she named it explicitly at 07:35-07:41. Bucket B5 (r2) is the one the transcript supports for this t; the في belongs to D1.

rows.r3_why: Both readers have the row; tier differs. فرق -> مختلف swaps the word (noun 'difference' for adjective 'different', different roots), which is the tier-1 definition; tier 2 is for a wrong form of the same word. Let-pass, so vocab-B.
